business_problem: Gilbert + Tobin wanted to improve client service and employee productivity while enabling a law firm to use AI safely with sensitive work and confidential client information.
solution_summary: Gilbert + Tobin moved from informal experimentation to controlled use of ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Work, and Codex, applying the tools to personal productivity and multistep workflows. The firm uses enterprise controls including Australian data residency, contractual protections, role-based access, and administrative oversight. CEO Sam Nickless built a custom GPT using writing examples, firm context, and feedback to help colleagues prepare ideas for discussion. ChatGPT Work was also used in a confidential annual review process for 120 partners to update files from spreadsheet data, create PDFs, and bundle completed materials. Codex and other OpenAI tools are part of the firm's move toward defined agentic workflows, with people responsible for reviewing outputs and approving final work. The firm reported active use by 87% of enabled ChatGPT users.

business_outcome: AI helped employees focus on client work, coaching, and judgment. The annual review file workflow was completed in minutes, and 87% of enabled ChatGPT users were active, more than twice the rate the firm typically saw for other tools.
